chinese: 古之善为道者，非以明民，将以愚之。
故以智治国，国之贼，不以智治国，国之福。
玄德深矣，远矣，与物反矣，然后乃至大顺。
pinyin: Gǔ zhī shàn wèi dào zhě， fēi yǐ míng mín， jiāng yǐ yú zhī。
Mín zhī nán zhì， yǐ qí zhì duō。
Gù yǐ zhì zhì guó， guó zhī zéi， bù yǐ zhì zhì guó， guó zhī fú。
Zhī cǐ liǎng zhě yì jī shì。
Cháng zhī jī shì， shì wèi xuán dé。
Xuán dé shēn yǐ， yuǎn yǐ， yǔ wù fǎn yǐ， rán hòu nǎi zhì dà shùn。
english: The ancient Masters who understood the way of the Tao, did not educate people, but made them forget.

Smart people are difficult to guide, because they think they are too clever. To use cleverness to rule a country, is to lead the country to ruin. To avoid cleverness in ruling a country, is to lead the country to prosperity.

Knowing the two alternatives is a pattern. Remaining aware of the pattern is a virtue. This dark and mysterious virtue is profound. It is opposite our natural inclination, but leads to harmony with the heavens.
